lines.text: Pumpkin head illusion. Dad dances back there, I hold the pumpkin up front. Boom, pumpkin head.
Nobody asked the pumpkin.
Patrice. You are a pumpkin. You do not get asked.
I have been in this patch for four months. I have seen things. I have standards.
I'm warmed up! I'm stretched! I did the hamstring thing in the car!
Is that the body? That is the body you picked for me?
Excuse me. I danced at three weddings this summer.
Dad, just show her the moves.
This is the sprinkler. This is the lawn mower. And this is the dad who found a twenty in his jacket.
Take one. Dad, go back by the hay bales. I'll hold her up. Ready? Dance!
Is it working? Do I look like a pumpkin?
No. You look like a tiny man standing next to a giant pumpkin.
I am not giant. I am confident.
Okay, further back. Now she looks like a grape on your shoulder.
Do not ever compare me to a grape. A grape has never been carried in a wagon.
Ma'am. You have to pay for the pumpkin before you put it on a man.
I am Gerald. I run the patch. Mostly I sit in the corn maze.
Big fan of the maze. We were in there for two hours.
It is eight rows of corn, sir.
We took the scenic way.
How much is she? We just need her for one video.
Pumpkins are by the pound. Dancing near a pumpkin is extra.
Depends on the dancing. Show me.
Okay. Here is the lawn mower, but it's going uphill.
That is going to cost you nine dollars.
Take two. Gerald, can you just stand very still and not be in the shot?
I am a bear in a field. I am always in the shot.
Okay, Dad, go! I'm holding her! It's lining up! It's perfect!
I am turning around.
Why would you turn around!
That is my bad side. You are not posting my bad side.
She has a bad side? She's round. She's all sides.
And all of them are better than the lawn mower.
I will hold the pumpkin. My arms are longer. I have done this before.
Every October. People come here and put Patrice on their dads. Every year she says no.
Patrice is not for sale. Patrice is my daughter.
Hi, Dad.
Your daughter is a pumpkin?
We found her in the patch. We do not use the word adopted. We use the word harvested.
Gerald, that's beautiful. I'm a girl dad too.
Then you know. Nobody puts your kid on a stranger's shoulders.
I put my kid on my shoulders at every parade until she was fourteen.
Wait. Hold on. I left the phone recording on the hay bale.
When Gerald held her up, she lined up perfectly. It's a bear doing the sprinkler. With a pumpkin head.
I was not dancing. I was waving off a bee.
Best video anyone has ever made of me. Finally, a body with standards.
So I came all the way out here to be the backup dad.
You can be in the next one, sir. That will be nine dollars.
Eighteen. He does the lawn mower again, it's eighteen.
